lobbying_activities.goal: Advocate for policies that maintain a competitive carbon pricing framework for Ontario industries, including alignment with federal carbon pricing systems and measures that prevent carbon leakage and ensure Ontario-based low-carbon fuel producers remain competitive with imported fuels produced under different regulatory regimes. Maintain support of the April 18, 2018/November 2020 amendments to the Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Park regulation (O. Reg 535/05) requiring fuel suppliers to maintain at least an annual average of 10% renewable content (such as ethanol) in the gasoline they sell in Ontario starting in 2020. Promote and incent the production and deployment of renewable natural gas, low carbon hydrogen and methanol in Ontario.

lobbying_activities.goal: As the leading biofuels and specialty alcohols manufacturer in Ontario, Greenfield will advocate for the effective implementation of low carbon fuels contemplated under the Made-in-Ontario Environment Plan. As an advanced biofuels technology provider, Greenfield will advocate for the funding to commercialize our technology, both locally and globally. Support policies that strengthen Ontario’s domestic supply chain for agricultural-based fermentation products, including ethanol and beverage alcohol inputs, in order to support Ontario farmers, maintain domestic production capacity, and ensure reliable supply for food, beverage, and fuel markets. Maintain and improve the standing of Ontario as an ethanol and biofuels-friendly jurisdiction. Promote the commercialization of next-generation biofuels and low-carbon fuels in Ontario, including renewable natural gas produced through anaerobic digestion, low-carbon hydrogen and methanol and sustainable aviation fuel. Support policies that strengthen Ontario’s agricultural bioeconomy, create value from agricultural by-products and organic waste streams, and expand domestic supply chains for fuel ethanol and fermentation-based industries.

lobbying_activities.goal: As the leading biofuels manufacturer in Ontario, Greenfield will advocate for the effective implementation of low carbon fuels contemplated under the Made-in-Ontario Environment Plan. As an advanced biofuels technology provider, Greenfield will advocate for the funding to commercialize our technology, both locally and globally. Support policies and programs that position Ontario as a leader in the bioeconomy by encouraging investment in low-carbon fuels and technologies including industrial fermentation and agricultural processing that create rural economic development and strengthen Ontario supply chains. To access existing and new funding programs and taxation policy to create an Advanced Biofuels cluster in the province of Ontario. Government regulations and programs that will incent the commercialization of renewable natural gas, low carbon hydrogen, methanol and sustainable aviation fuel for use in the province of Ontario and to meet growing demand both nationally and globally.
